prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but I don’t have live browsing access, so I can’t pull current names and ratings for Joplin businesses right now. I can, however, quickly help you find a reliable contractor and give a vetted checklist to pick one. To give a specific recommendation I can look up current options if you want to paste a few names/links you’ve found — or tell me the project type and I’ll tell you exactly how to find and vet the best local candidates.

Quick plan and resources
- Search local listings: Google Maps (search “home remodel contractor Joplin, MO”), Angi (Angie’s List), Houzz, HomeAdvisor, Thumbtack, Yelp.
- Check complaints/reputation: Better Business Bureau (BBB.org), Google Reviews, Facebook community groups / Nextdoor.
- Local sources: Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce, local real estate agents, building supply stores (they often recommend reliable subs), and recent neighbors who’ve done similar jobs.

What to verify before hiring
1. License & permits
   - Ask whether the work requires local permits and who will pull them. Confirm any required local registration or trade license.
2. Insurance
   - Confirm general liability and workers’ compensation coverage. Ask for certificates naming you as interested party if requested.
3. References & portfolio
   - Ask for recent projects of the same type and contact information for at least 2 former clients. Inspect photos or visit a finished job if possible.
4. Written estimate & contract
   - Get at least 2–3 written bids that itemize labor, materials, allowances, timeline, and payment schedule. The contract should include scope, start/finish dates, warranty, change order process, and insurance info.
5. Payments & schedule
   - Avoid large up-front payments. Typical down payments vary by job size (commonly 10–30%), with balance tied to milestones. Never pay in full up front.
6. Warranties & lien releases
   - Get written warranties on work and materials. Require lien waivers on milestone payments to protect against subcontractor claims.
7. Red flags
   - No contract, only cash payments, unusually low bids, poor communication, unwillingness to provide references or proof of insurance.

Questions to ask a contractor (short script)
- “Are you licensed/registered in Joplin/Missouri for this type of work?”
- “Can you provide proof of liability and workers’ comp insurance?”
- “Can you provide 2–3 recent references and photos of similar projects?”
- “Who will supervise the job day-to-day, and who will be my point of contact?”
- “What is your projected start and completion date, and what’s your payment schedule?”
- “How do you handle changes during the project and warranties after completion?”

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft an outreach message to contractors.
- Create a short comparison worksheet for bids.
- Evaluate 2–3 contractor quotes or profiles if you paste them here.
- Look up likely local companies if you give me permission to run a web search (I’d need you to paste results, because I can’t browse).

Tell me the project type (kitchen, bath, whole-house remodel, roof, siding, deck, general repairs), rough budget, and whether you prefer small local firms vs. larger remodelers — I’ll tailor the next steps and a shortlist process for you.
